what_happened: The job "Steward steps back and decides itself; asks owner only for env or token" (prompts) was rejected. The verifier said the reading misread the request. It marked 2 of 6 acceptance criteria unmet: the cargo test criterion (a roles.rs prompt test plus a steward.rs test that an item needing no environment or token gets no brief, while one that does keeps its five-field brief), and the clippy/fmt/token-budget criterion. It gave 5 blocker or major findings. (1) The env/token case never reaches the owner as a brief (steward.rs:708-712, 739-749). (2) Proposals above the limit still go to the owner, now without a brief (work_decisions.rs:43-51). (3) The new steward prompt likely exceeds the 600-token Steward budget, and no test checks the real prompt. (4) The required brief-with/without-need test is missing. (5) The reading does not match the request, so passing criteria do not show the request was met. No check failed; the unmet items are criteria and the findings are verifier judgments.
cause: The steward's behavior is set partly by its prompt and partly by code (briefing and limit routing in steward.rs and work_decisions.rs). The reading treated the request as a prompt wording change and did not trace where briefs are made or where over-limit proposals go. The Steward prompt also has a tight token budget, and nothing measured the remaining room before the plan. Criteria checked that the prompt names the exception and that a test exists, not that the owner-routing behavior changes. Nothing cross-checks a reading against the code that enforces the behavior before the producer runs, so the gap surfaces only at the final verdict.
prevention: Add a reading-stage step for requests that change an agent's decision rule. The reader must name each code path that consumes the agent's output (briefing, limit routing) and state which change each needs. It must also record the prompt's remaining token room, measured from the real prompt. Each criterion must then demonstrate the behavior end to end: an item with no env/token need reaches no owner brief, an item with one gets the five-field brief, and over-limit proposals follow the intended route. A budget test must run on the real prompt text. The critic should reject a reading whose criteria only check that the prompt wording exists.
proposed_request: Make the Steward decide on its own and ask the owner only when an item needs an environment or token the Steward cannot supply. Outcome: an item that needs no environment or token produces no owner brief and is decided by the Steward. An item that does need one still reaches the owner with its five-field brief. Proposals above the limit follow the existing limit rule and must not reach the owner without a brief. Before the plan, trace the code that builds briefs and routes items to the owner (crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs and work_decisions.rs) and change whatever enforces this there, not only the prompt. Update the Steward prompt in crates/athena-data/src/roles.rs so it names stepping back and the env/token exception, and keep it within the 600-token Steward budget, measured on the real prompt text. Acceptance: (1) a steward.rs test shows an item with no env or token need gets no brief, and one with the need keeps its five-field brief; (2) a test shows an over-limit proposal is routed as intended; (3) a roles.rs test asserts the prompt names the step back and the exception, and the real prompt fits the budget; (4) cargo test -p athena-data -p athena-core -p athena-cli, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check all pass; (5) add the CHANGELOG.md entry and amend any decision in docs/decisions.md that describes the old Steward behavior.
